_about: Hand-kept facts about each defect that the test run cannot know: who fixed it, how, and any proposal for the team. The STATUS, RETEST RESULT and DATE CLOSED are never written here: scripts/fill_final_workbook.py works them out from the latest run of tests/test_final_cases.py (a defect closes only when every linked case passes). D-01 to D-12 keep the description, steps, severity and date recorded in the team workbook on 29 Sep; D-13 onwards were found on v2 during this work. 'fix_commits' are git log --grep patterns on commit subjects; the filler turns them into commit hashes. A 'proposal' is never an acceptance: accepting a defect is the team's call.

D-01.fixed_by: v2 build (canon() in src/url_features.py strips the scheme, a leading www. and a trailing slash in training and serving)
D-01.fix_summary: v2 canonicalises every URL the same way in training and serving, so https:// and a trailing slash no longer change the score (URL-05, URL-06). The remaining failure is U-H06 in URL-07: a real Google sign-in URL with a long query. That is the login-page trade-off results.md describes, not the scheme fault. Phase 3.2 retrains only if the scheme or slash still flips labels, and it does not.

D-02.fixed_by: v2 build (empty text gives HTTP 422) and this work
D-02.fix_summary: Empty text was already refused with HTTP 422 in v2. /score and /correlate now also refuse malformed URLs and unknown channels with HTTP 422 and a message that says why (check_url in src/url_features.py).

D-03.fix_summary: An empty request is refused with HTTP 422. A bundle whose events cannot be assessed (calls, voice, video, or a channel whose model is missing) answers status CANNOT_ASSESS with no risk and the label 'cannot assess', never a low score.

D-04.fixed_by: v2 build (60-minute window, DEFAULT_WINDOW_MIN in src/fusion.py)
D-04.fix_summary: Events further apart than the window (60 minutes) are not combined or linked. Each window is scored on its own and the bundle takes the highest.

D-05.fixed_by: v2 build (tldextract with its bundled public suffix list)
D-05.fix_summary: Domains are matched on the full public suffix list, so .online and .co.in hosts link events.

D-06.fixed_by: this work (v2 had CORS open to '*')
D-06.fix_summary: CORS names the console's development origins (localhost:5173 and 127.0.0.1:5173, CP1_CORS_ORIGINS to change) and never '*'. The built console is served by the API itself, so it needs no CORS.

D-07.fix_summary: A 'time' that is not a number or an ISO timestamp gives HTTP 422 with the event number, not a 500.

D-08.fixed_by: v2 build (identity tokens are domains, phone numbers and the identity field only)
D-08.fix_summary: Ordinary words are never identity tokens.

D-09.fixed_by: v2 build (three-class SMS model trained on the LSDST smishing corpus)
D-09.fix_summary: The fault described here, missed phishing SMS, no longer shows: SMS-01 catches every standard phishing SMS. SMS-03 still fails, but on its legitimate half (bank alerts flagged), which is D-16. The case cannot pass, and so this defect cannot close, until D-16 is fixed.

D-10.fix_summary: EML-02 passes on v2. EML-03 still fails: one hard legitimate email (E-H04) is flagged, and one hard phishing email is missed (D-17). Phase 3.1 retrains the email model with real phishing corpora.

D-11.fix_summary: clean_text() drops script, style, head and title blocks with their content, keeps link targets as URLs, and strips only real tags. Training uses the same cleaner, so the email model is retrained in Phase 3.

D-12.fix_summary: S-01, S-02 and S-11 already alert on a single channel with the real models, so correlation cannot raise their verdict. TC-06, a hand-written case with real scores, is lifted over the line by correlation and its control TC-07 is not (tests/test_demo_cases.py); the simulated weak campaigns are in reports/window_metrics.json. The R2-09 evidence table (Phase 2.5) puts these side by side.
D-12.proposal: Proposed: accept because no case in S-01, S-02 or S-11 can show a lift (each already alerts alone), and the lift is shown instead by TC-06 against TC-07. This stays a hand-written and simulated result until real bundles exist (R2-10).

D-13.description: On v2, /correlate refuses the whole bundle with HTTP 501 when any one event is a call or a video. The email and SMS in the same bundle are never scored.
D-13.steps: POST /correlate with an email event and a channel='video' event. v2 answers HTTP 501.
D-13.fix_summary: Call, voice and video events are returned as 'not assessed' (score null, with the reason) and kept out of the fusion features, the shared tokens and the window. The rest of the bundle is scored as before.

D-14.description: On v2, the API does not start when one model file is missing (FileNotFoundError at import). There is no degraded mode.
D-14.steps: Remove models/sms_model.joblib (in a copy) and start the API.
D-14.fix_summary: Each model loads on its own. A missing one makes only that channel unavailable: /health says 'degraded', /score answers 503 for it, and /correlate lists its events as not assessed.

D-15.description: clean_text(123) returns '123'. The plan expects an empty string for any input that is not text.
D-15.fix_summary: clean_text() returns an empty string for anything that is not a string.

D-16.description: The SMS model flags legitimate transactional bank SMS: the card-use alert S-H05 and the bill reminder S-H08 in the hard group, and the credit alert S-L05 in the standard group (SMS-02 still meets its target). Scores are in the Data-SMS sheet.
D-16.steps: POST S-H05, S-H08 and S-L05 to /score with channel=sms.
D-16.fix_summary: Needs retraining with more legitimate transactional SMS (Phase 3.3), from a source whose licence can be checked.

D-17.description: The email model misses standard phishing emails that the old build caught: E-P03 (password expiry), E-P06 (fake invoice), E-P07 (gift-card CEO fraud) and E-P09 (fake job offer), and the hard case E-H01. results.md limitation 1 says why: the training corpora hold spam and fraud, not real phishing email.
D-17.steps: POST E-P03, E-P06, E-P07, E-P09 and E-H01 to /score with channel=email.
D-17.fix_summary: Phase 3.1 adds the Nazario, SpamAssassin and Ling corpora and retrains under the adoption rule.

D-18.description: The learned correlation model can give a bundle less risk than its strongest event when the other events in the window are weaker: in S-06 the email alone scores higher than the bundle, and in TC-04 (UI-03) the bundle shows 99.99% beside an SMS at 100.00%. The alert does not change in either case.
D-18.steps: POST S-06 (phishing email, harmless SMS and URL) to /correlate and compare bundle_risk with the email's score.
D-18.fix_summary: This is how the learned model lowers false alarms: when a high score sits beside benign events it may pull the bundle down. A floor at the best single score would bring back single-channel alerting and its false alarms (reports/window_metrics.json).
D-18.proposal: Proposed: accept because the alert does not change in S-06, and lowering a lone high score next to benign events is where the model's lower false-alarm rate on simulated bundles comes from. Recheck on real bundles (R2-10).
